original.reason: The claimed factorial argument does not establish gaps in S: composite numbers need not fail to be one less than a prime, and the listed set does not yield the asserted interval. Moreover, Claim 1 improperly concludes all non-selected destinations are N using only an induction hypothesis that earlier selected values are P; this is circular because Claim 2 has not yet been proved.

judgment.reason: It correctly obtains arbitrarily long omitted intervals in S from predecessors of consecutive composite numbers, proves the greedy sequence continues, and gives a sound strong induction classifying exactly the selected values as P-positions.
